primitives.assumptions: Behavioral transitions are deterministic within a fixed instinctual framework; impulses arise from internal state changes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When external stimuli exceed innate thresholds, leading to adaptive deviation or maladaptive rigidity.

primitives.name: Impulse Chain Determinism
primitives.verbatim_quote: In certain animals of a low order the feeling of having executed one impulsive step is such an indispensable part of the stimulus of the next one, that the animal cannot make any variation in the order of its performance.
primitives.assumptions: Sequential actions form a deterministic chain where prior action is necessary condition for subsequent action.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Disruption of sensory-motor feedback loop leads to loss of sequential integrity and behavioral stereotypy.

layer2.mapping: Markovian process A(t+1) = g(A(t), E(t)) mirrors neural circuitry encoding stimulus-response chains.
layer2.telemetry: Repetitive action pattern fidelity across multiple trials under identical environmental conditions.

primitives.name: Behavioral Utility Preference
primitives.verbatim_quote: But it is not for the sake of their utility that they are followed, but because at the moment of following them we feel that that is the only appropriate and natural thing to do.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'U': 'utility preference (dimensionless)', 'F': 'feeling of appropriateness (arbitrary units)', 'B': 'behavioral choice (set of options)'}
primitives.assumptions: Preference is driven by affective states rather than rational cost-benefit analysis.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When emotional regulation fails, leading to irrational or compulsive behavioral choices.

layer2.mapping: Utility maximization U(B) = h(F) reflects subjective valuation derived from affective feedback loops.
layer2.telemetry: Subjective self-reporting of behavioral satisfaction and repetition frequency.

Failure modes include rigid adherence to obsolete impulses, breakdown in sequential behavior due to disrupted feedback, and irrational choices driven by affective misalignment.
